Female-Dominated Teams Help Women Get Ahead In Science

A team of psychologists report on an intervention for college undergraduates which found that female first-year students participate more actively and feel less anxious when they are able to work in small groups or "microenvironments" that are mostly female.

This is interesting. But I wonder how much of this is due to the stereotype threat and other issues of discrimination or differences in societal/cultural behavior and how much is just a gender difference in working and collaboration styles and effectiveness.

The degree to which this is an issue of conditioning across the women's lives vs how much is an innate gender difference, on average, is an important factor in the continued discussion of equality of opportunity vs equality of results.
